stem: An adult client has a short-term central venous catheter covered with a sterile transparent semipermeable dressing. When should the dressing be replaced according to CDC guidance?

options.A: At least every 7 days, and sooner if it becomes damp, loose, or visibly soiled
options.B: Only when the catheter itself is removed
options.C: Every 24 hours regardless of dressing condition
options.D: Once each month if the dressing remains attached

rationale: CDC catheter-related infection prevention guidance recommends replacing transparent dressings used on short-term central venous catheter sites at least every 7 days, except when pediatric dislodgement risk outweighs the benefit. Any catheter-site dressing should be replaced sooner if it becomes damp, loosened, or visibly soiled.
educational_objective: Apply CDC central-line dressing intervals by replacing transparent short-term CVC dressings at least every 7 days and sooner when compromised.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_document_title: Guidelines for the Prevention of Intravascular Catheter-Related Infections — Summary of Recommendations
source_locator: Section 6 Catheter Site Dressing Regimens, Recommendations 3 and 7
source_claim_supported: Replace a catheter-site dressing if damp, loosened, or visibly soiled; replace transparent dressings on short-term CVC sites at least every 7 days, with a pediatric dislodgement-risk exception.
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
correction_summary: Corrected the original 5-7 day range to the exact CDC short-term CVC recommendation of at least every 7 days, while retaining the earlier-change criteria for a compromised dressing.
audit_findings: A combines the exact routine interval and compromised-dressing indications. B, C, and D contradict CDC guidance. Adult status removes the pediatric exception from the decision.
